key_insight: E-3DPSM introduces a state-machine architecture that models the asynchronous, continuous nature of event-camera streams to produce substantially more accurate egocentric 3D human poses from head-mounted devices. By explicitly handling event timing and temporal states, it closes the accuracy gap required for immersive AR/VR applications.
problem_solved: Existing monocular egocentric 3D pose methods do not fully exploit the asynchronous, high-temporal-resolution structure of event-camera data, yielding insufficient 3D accuracy and unstable tracking for real-time immersive use.
method: State-machine driven processing that organizes event streams into meaningful temporal states (e.g., motion onset, steady motion, rest) to preserve asynchronous timing and reduce information loss.
Spatiotemporal feature extraction tailored to event data and a regression module that maps state-aware features to 3D joint positions with temporal/kinematic consistency constraints.
Training and evaluation strategy combining event-specific augmentations and losses to improve robustness to occlusions, fast motion, and varying illumination common in head-mounted setups.
impact: Provides a practical path to low-latency, high-accuracy egocentric 3D pose estimation using event cameras, enabling more responsive and immersive AR/VR experiences and informing future event-based perception models in robotics and HCI.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing event-camera input → state machine (temporal states) → spatiotemporal feature extractor → 3D pose output.
Side-by-side visualization comparing raw event stream vs. conventional frame data to highlight temporal resolution and reduced motion blur.
Performance chart (accuracy vs. latency) showing E-3DPSM improvement over baseline methods.
Schematic of head-mounted camera and inferred 3D skeleton in an AR scene to convey application and egocentric viewpoint.
paper_title: E-3DPSM: A State Machine for Event-Based Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Mayur Deshmukh, Hiroyasu Akada, Helge Rhodin, Christian Theobalt, Vladislav Golyanik
